newsitem.title: USA: Albany Cty, N.Y., official derails bond sale - paper.
newsitem.headline: Albany Cty, N.Y., official derails bond sale - paper.

text.p: The comptroller of Albany County, N.Y., failed to approve a proposed $110 million bond sale planned for January 13 for the local airport, the Albany Times Union said in its Tuesday edition.
The sale of revenue bonds to finance a $158 million expansion had been unanimously approved by the Albany County Airport Authority.

However, the paper said Michael Conners, county comptroller, objected to several aspects of the deal, including its 30-year term, saying a 20-year maturity might be less costly. He also has opposed airport plans to sell the bonds through negotiation instead of competition, the paper said.
The bond sale must be approved by both Conners and the state comptroller. The airport chief executive officer said he expected the state comptroller to soon approve the bond sale.
As an alternative, Conners proposed the county issue debt to cover $865,000 in airport expansion costs for 1997, while he finishes his review, the paper said.
